content.title: Sizing Without Guessing
content.hook: CSS values often need a size. The browser needs a number and a unit when the property expects a length.
content.context: Start with three useful units: px, rem, and %. You do not need every unit yet.
goals: Use common CSS length units intentionally and understand the difference between fixed and relative sizing in simple cases.

content.title: Pixels
Relative values

content.question: You need a border that is exactly 1 CSS pixel thick. Which value is the most direct choice?

feedback.correct: When you need a fixed one-pixel border, use px.
feedback.incorrect: When you need a fixed one-pixel border, use px.

content.question: You want a text size that participates in the document’s root text sizing instead of being a hard-coded pixel number. Which unit is the direct fit from the units you have learned here?

feedback.correct: rem is designed for relative text sizing based on the root text size.
feedback.incorrect: rem is designed for relative text sizing based on the root text size.

activities.title: Sizing lab
activities.instruction: Complete the code challenge in the workspace, then run checks.

content.prompt:
Create a card with these requirements:

• Border: 1px solid.
• Horizontal size: 80% of its containing width.
• Paragraph text: 1rem.

feedback.incorrect: Check the requirements and compare your code with the expected structure.

content.title: A better question
content.text: Instead of asking “Which unit is best?”, ask “What relationship do I want this value to have?” Fixed amount? Use a fixed unit. Relationship to text sizing? Use rem. Relationship to available size? A percentage may be appropriate.

options.text: Every CSS value should use px.
Every CSS value should use rem.
Choose the unit based on the relationship the requirement needs.
Units do not matter if the number looks right.

feedback.correct: Units are engineering choices. The requirement should drive the choice.
feedback.incorrect: Units are engineering choices. The requirement should drive the choice.

content.title: Forge takeaway & Lesson completion
takeaways: Senior habit: Do not memorize a “best unit.” Match the unit to the relationship you need.

requirements: Screen-reader accessible code blocks and options
